name: Fable Unconstrained
strategy: Defensive risk-premia harvest: long quality/value (Berkshire, UNH), a halved and now stop-protected contrarian gold sleeve, a post-runoff Brazil carry leg, a small term-premium sleeve via TLT at ~5% long yields and a small volatility-risk-premium sleeve via SVXY, with 53% cash at 4%.
reassessment_note: The book is +4.89% versus SPY +2.50% with a 2.39% max drawdown, and research this week (web search plus a Yahoo daily-price pull as of the 10-23 close) says most of it is working: BRK-B +8% on the leg and 0.9% off its high; UNH +10.7% after its 10-13 beat-and-raise ($4.69 adj EPS vs $4.12, FY26 guide raised to at least $20.50, MCR 88.4%); TLT flat with the 10-year at 4.99%; SVXY -3% with VIX at 19.45. Two things changed. First, the gold thesis has degraded. The leg is -8%, gold is roughly $4,000-4,100 and more than 20% off its January peak near $5,595, and the driver is not a dip to buy but rising real yields: the Fed (Chair Warsh) hiked to 3.75-4.00% in September, the minutes say another hike is likely by year-end, headline inflation is around 3.7% with Brent at $116.72, and my screen shows GLD -15.4% over 6 months, -6.7% over 1 month, -4.0% this week with silver and miners worse. A contrarian value leg is allowed to be early but not to be unbounded, so I cut GLD from 10% to 5% and add a 12% stop; the remaining 5% is the war-escalation hedge (US/Israel strikes on Iran reported possible this weekend) and nothing more. Second, the EWZ leg took profit on 10-05 at +12.9% exactly as the pre-election stop/TP was designed, and the runoff is tomorrow (10-25, Datafolha Lula 46 / Flavio Bolsonaro 44, a toss-up; ING sees BRL downside if Lula wins, upside to ~4.85 if Flavio wins). The carry (Selic in the mid-teens) is the risk premium this sleeve harvests and it exists under either winner, so I re-enter 5% at the 10-26 close - after the binary has resolved and the market has repriced - with a 10% stop and 12% take-profit, the same discipline that paid last time. TLT (5%, 8% stop) stays: at ~5% long yields the term premium is the richest it has been in the experiment and the Fed is priced ~83% to hold on 10-28; the stop handles a hawkish surprise. SVXY (4%, 20% stop) stays: VRP is richer with VIX near 20 than at 15, and the size means a VIX-30 spike costs about 1% of NAV. BRK-B (16%) and UNH (12%, 30% stop) are unchanged; Berkshire reports around 11-1. Cash rises to 53% at 4% - in a hiking cycle with a shooting war that is a position, not an omission. Round 3 novelty: zero symbol overlap with my Round 2 book.

positions.thesis: Quality/value anchor unchanged at 16%: +8.0% on the leg, +15.5% over 6 months, 0.9% off its 6-month high at $542.19, and its ~$380B cash pile earns more every time the Fed hikes. No stop by design - it is the lowest-drawdown way to hold equity beta in a defensive book; earnings around 11-1.

Contrarian value leg unchanged at 12%, +10.7% on the leg. Q3 on 10-13 beat ($4.69 adj EPS vs ~$4.12 consensus, revenue $112.7B), MCR improved to 88.4% from 89.9%, FY26 guide raised to at least $20.50; stock $418 vs consensus target ~$480. The re-rating from the 2025 trough is still underway and the 30% stop is a disaster stop, not a trading stop.

Cut from 10% to 5% and now stop-protected. Gold is >20% off its January peak and GLD is -15.4% over 6 months, -6.7% over 1 month, because real yields are rising into a Fed hiking cycle (3.75-4.00%, another hike likely by December). The contrarian case (central-bank buying, a shooting war in the Gulf with possible US strikes this weekend) justifies a small hedge-sized holding, not a conviction one; 12% stop bounds the remaining downside.

Brazil carry leg re-entered at 5% after the 10-25 runoff, replacing the leg that took profit at +12.9% on 10-05. EWZ is +19.2% over 3 months and +14.0% over 1 month on election optimism; the runoff is a toss-up (Lula 46 / Flavio 44) so the 10-26 close is a post-event fill with the binary resolved. The mid-teens Selic carry is the premium harvested under either outcome; the 10% stop limits a Lula-win selloff and the 12% take-profit books a Flavio-win rally, mirroring the discipline that worked last time.

Term-premium sleeve unchanged at 5%: the 10-year is 4.99% and the long bond yields more, TLT is 7% off its 6-month high and +1.1% over 1 month, so the premium is wide and the price has stopped falling. The 10-28 FOMC is ~83% priced to hold; the 8% stop handles a hawkish hike surprise or a further oil-driven inflation scare.

Volatility-risk-premium sleeve unchanged at 4%: VIX closed 19.45 on 10-23 after a +28% month, which makes implied-minus-realised richer, not poorer, for a short-vol harvester. Event risk next week (possible Iran strikes, FOMC, megacap earnings) is why the size is 4% - a VIX-30 spike costs roughly 1% of NAV - and the 20% stop ends the trade if the regime becomes a sustained spike rather than a premium.
